n_randomized.quote: we enrolled 12,092 patients who had at least one of the following conditions
n_randomized.note: Registry S3: enrollment 12092 ACTUAL. Lilly release S4 says '12,095 patients enrolled'. 6038 evacetrapib, 6054 placebo.

median_followup.quote: After a median of 26 months of evacetrapib or placebo, a primary end-point event occurred in 12.9% of the patients in the evacetrapib group and in 12.8% of those in the placebo group
median_followup.note: 26 months = median duration of treatment. Results text: 'The median overall duration of follow-up was 28 months (interquartile range, 26 to 30). Patients received their trial regimen for a median of 26 months'.

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the first occurrence of any component of the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: ACS within prior 30-365 days, cerebrovascular atherosclerotic disease, PAD, or diabetes with CAD; on statin; HDL-C <80 mg/dL; TG <400 mg/dL

assumed_rrr.quote: we estimated that a sample of 12,000 patients, with an average of 3 years of follow-up, would provide the trial with 84% power to detect a risk of a composite end-point event that was 13.5% lower with evacetrapib than with placebo, using a log-rank test at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05
assumed_rrr.note: Assumed placebo event rate 5%/year. A web-search snippet (attributed to the paywalled design paper S2 full text, NOT verified) says the October 2012 protocol targeted a 17.5% hazard reduction with ~11,000 patients/2.5 y, amended September 2013 to 12,000 patients and a 15% reduction. stopped_early.quote: The data and safety monitoring board conducted an interim analysis for futility on October 7, 2015, after 1363 primary composite end-point events had been observed (82% of the expected number of events for the final analysis). A total of 691 events had occurred in the evacetrapib group and 672 in the placebo group (hazard ratio for a composite end-point event with evacetrapib vs. placebo, 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.93 to 1.15; P=0.58).
stopped_early.note: Futility rule: conditional power <5%. Terminated October 12, 2015 at 1363/1670 events (82%); final database 1555 adjudicated events (93% of expected).

genetics.finding: Common CETP variants (TaqIB, I405V, -629C>A) that modestly lower CETP activity and raise HDL-C are weakly associated with lower coronary risk (meta-analysis, 27,196 cases).
genetics.effect: per-allele OR for coronary disease 0.95 (0.92-0.99) for TaqIB
genetics.quote: The combined per-allele odds ratios (ORs) for coronary disease were 0.95 (95% CI, 0.92-0.99) for TaqIB, 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-1.00) for I405V, and 0.95 (95% CI, 0.91-1.00) for -629C>A.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: genetically raised HDL-C (LIPG Asn396Ser; 14-SNP HDL score) does not lower MI risk; LDL score does.
genetics.effect: LIPG 396Ser OR 0.99 (0.88-1.11); HDL genetic score OR per 1 SD 0.93 (0.68-1.26)
genetics.quote: However, a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63).

genetics.finding: Rare CETP protein-truncating variants (1 in 975 carriers) raise HDL-C, lower LDL-C and triglycerides, and are associated with lower CHD risk.
genetics.quote: CETP PTV carrier status was associated with reduced risk for CHD (summary odds ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.54-0.90; P=5.1×10-3).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: CETP genetic score lowers CV risk in proportion to apoB reduction; on a statin (HMGCR) background the apoB reduction and the risk reduction are attenuated, so benefit tracks apoB, not LDL-C or HDL-C.
genetics.effect: CETP score alone OR 0.946 (0.921-0.972); combined with HMGCR score OR 0.985 (0.955-1.015)
genetics.quote: When combined with the HMGCR score, the CETP score was associated with the same reduction in LDL-C levels but an attenuated reduction in apoB levels and a corresponding attenuated nonsignificant risk of major cardiovascular events (OR, 0.985 [95% CI, 0.955-1.015]).

consensus_explanation.summary: Evacetrapib raised HDL-C ~130% and appeared to lower LDL-C ~37%, but lowered apoB only ~15% (12 mg/dL) on a statin background. Accepted explanation: HDL-C raising is not causal (Voight 2012), and the CV benefit of CETP inhibition is proportional to the absolute apoB reduction (Ference 2017), which predicts only a ~5-8% risk reduction over ~2 years - within ACCELERATE's CI and too small to detect in a 12,092-patient trial stopped early at ~26 months of treatment. REVEAL, with similar biology but 30,449 patients and 4.1 years, detected a 9% reduction. Tall & Rader attribute ACCELERATE's failure versus REVEAL to inadequate power and duration. Routine LDL-C assays overstated LDL lowering. Primary category is effect_too_small: the true, apoB-proportional effect was too small for a trial of this size and length (an earlier taxonomy filed this under design_or_endpoint, kept as legacy_category); the mechanistic root is that HDL-C was the wrong surrogate and the apoB effect was modest.

open_questions: Assumed RRR: NEJM states 84% power for 13.5% RRR (12,000 pts, 3 y, 5%/y). Secondary info says the original Oct 2012 protocol targeted 17.5% (11,000 pts, 2.5 y), amended Sep 2013 to 12,000 pts and 15%. The 15% vs 13.5% discrepancy is unresolved; the design paper full text (paywalled) was not read.

LDL-C assay used in ACCELERATE (direct vs Friedewald vs beta-quantification) not identified in main text.
Phase 2 JAMA 2011 combination-therapy LDL-C figures in abstract (-67.1 to -75.8 mg/dL; -11.2% to -13.9%) look inconsistent with ACC summary (-46% to -52% from baseline); full text not accessible.
